chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me said: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Harith ibn al-Dalhath, the freedman of Al-Rida (peace be upon him), said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say:
The believer is not a true believer until there are three characteristics in him: a Sunnah from his Lord, a Sunnah from his Prophet, and a Sunnah from his Guardian (Imam),
so the Sunnah from his Lord is guarding his secret,
God, the Mighty and Majestic, said: 'He (alone) knows the Unseen, so He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except whom He chooses of a Messenger.'
And as for the Sunnah from his Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), it is courting the people (kind treatment),

for God, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to court the people, saying: 'Take what is given freely, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.'
And as for the Sunnah from his Guardian, it is patience in hardship and adversity,
for God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And those who are patient in hardship and adversity.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three characteristics that make a believer truly faithful according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents a hierarchical model of spiritual perfection where the believer's conduct mirrors the divine attributes of the Prophet and the Imam, emphasizing the integration of esoteric knowledge (kumun al-sirr) with social grace (mudarata). This triad reflects the Shia understanding of the Imam as the living embodiment of the Sunnah, guiding the faithful through the practical application of patience (sabr) in both adversity and prosperity. The hadith thus bridges metaphysical reality with ethical behavior, establishing the Imam's role as the essential link between the Prophet's teachings and the believer's daily life.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-7 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad , on the authority of Sahl ibn Zyad, on the authority of Al-Harith ibn al-Dalhath - a servant of Al-Ridha (MGB), “I heard Abal-Hassan (MGB)say
‘One cannot be a true believer unless he possesses the following three characteristics: one from his Lord, one from his Prophet and one from his Imam.
The one from his Lord is guarding secrets
as the Honorable the Exalted God said, ‘He (alone) knows the Unseen, nor does He make anyone acquainted with his Mysteries, except an Apostle whom He has chosen.’
However, the one from the Prophet is kind treatment with the people,
as the Honorable the Exalted God has ordered His Prophet (MGB) to treat the people with kindness and patience and said, ‘Hold to forgiveness; command what is right; but turn away from the ignorant.’
And the one from the Imams (MGB) is patience and perseverance during times of hardship and calamities.
The Honorable the Exalted God says, ‘…and to be firm and patient, in pain (or suffering) and adversity…’ ”
